[flags]\n\nFlags:\nINPUT:\n   -l, -list string              input file containing list of hosts to process\n   -rr, -request string          file containing raw request\n   -u, -target string[]          input target host(s) to probe\n   -im, -input-mode string       mode of input file (burp)\n\nPROBES:\n   -sc, -status-code                      display response status-code\n   -cl, -content-length                   display response content-length\n   -ct, -content-type                     display response content-type\n   -location                              display response redirect location\n   -favicon                               display mmh3 hash for '/favicon.ico' file\n   -hash string                           display response body hash (supported: md5,mmh3,simhash,sha1,sha256,sha512)\n   -jarm                                  display jarm fingerprint hash\n   -rt, -response-time                    display response time\n   -lc, -line-count                       display response body line count\n   -wc, -word-count                       display response body word count\n   -title                                 display page title\n   -bp, display technology in use based on wappalyzer dataset\n   -cff, -custom-fingerprint-file string  path to a custom fingerprint file for technology detection\n   -method                                display http request method\n   -ws, -websocket                        display server using websocket\n   -ip                                    display host ip\n   -cname                                 display host cname\n   -extract-fqdn, -efqdn                  get domain and subdomains from response body and header in jsonl/csv output\n   -asn                                   display host asn       enable saving screenshot of the page using headless browser\n   -system-chrome                   enable using local installed chrome for screenshot\n   -ho, -headless-options string[]  start respect HSTS response headers for redirect requests\n   -vhost-input                     get a list of vhosts as input\n   -x string                        request methods to probe, use 'all' to probe <p dir="auto">
<code>httpx</code>
 is a fast and multi-purpose HTTP toolkit that allows running multiple probes using the 
<a href="https://github.com/projectdiscovery/retryablehttp-go">retryablehttp</a>
 library. It is designed to maintain result reliability with an increased number of threads.
</p>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>
Simple and modular code base making it easy to contribute.
</li>
<li>
Fast And fully configurable flags to probe multiple elements.
</li>
<li>
Supports multiple HTTP based probings.
</li>
<li>
Smart auto fallback from https to http by default.
</li>
<li>
Supports hosts, URLs and CIDR as input.
</li>
<li>
Handles edge cases doing retries, backoffs etc for handling WAFs.
</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">This will display help for the tool. Here are all the switches it supports.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-text-shell-session notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-c1">httpx is a fast and multi-purpose HTTP toolkit that allows running multiple probes using the retryablehttp library.</span>

<span class="pl-c1">Usage:</span>
<span class="pl-c1">  ./httpx [flags]</span>

<span class="pl-c1">Flags:</span>
<span class="pl-c1">INPUT:</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -l, -list string              input file containing list of hosts to process</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -rr, -request string          file containing raw request</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -u, -target string[]          input target host(s) to probe</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -im, -input-mode string       mode of input file (burp)</span>

<span class="pl-c1">PROBES:</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -sc, -status-code                      display response status-code</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -cl, -content-length                   display response content-length</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -ct, -content-type                     display response content-type</span>
<span class="pl-c1">   -location                              display response redirect location</span>

<p dir="auto">
<code>httpx</code>
 can be used as a library by creating an instance of the 
<code>Option</code>
 struct and populating it with the same options that would be specified via CLI. Once validated, the struct should be passed to a runner instance (to be closed at the end of the program) and the 
<code>RunEnumeration</code>
 method should be called. A minimal example of how to do it is in the 
<a href="/projectdiscovery/httpx/blob/dev/examples">examples</a>
 folder.
</p>

<p dir="auto">
Below are practical one-liners for common use cases leveraging httpx's composable primitives. These recipes are validated in 
<code>runner/wellknown_recipes_test.go</code>
.

<p dir="auto">
Use 
<code>-mdc</code>
 with DSL helpers such as 
<code>contains(content_type, ...)</code>
 and 
<code>contains(body, ...)</code>
 to match response metadata and body content. (
<code>-mr</code>
/
<code>-ms</code>
 match the full raw response; use 
<code>-mdc</code>
 for structured field matching.)
</p>

<p dir="auto">
<strong>security.txt</strong>
<br>

Probe for a valid 
<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9116.html" rel="nofollow">RFC 9116</a>
 security.txt file at the standard paths (
<code>/.well-known/security.txt</code>
, 
<code>/security.txt</code>
):
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-c1">echo</span>
 target.com 
<span class="pl-k">|</span>
 httpx -path 
<span class="pl-s">
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
/.well-known/security.txt,/security.txt
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
</span>
 -mc 200 -mdc 
<span class="pl-s">
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
contains(content_type, "text/plain") && contains(body, "Contact:") && contains_any(body, "mailto:", "https://")
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
</span>
</pre>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>
As default, 
<code>httpx</code>
 probe with 
<strong>HTTPS</strong>
 scheme and fall-back to 
<strong>HTTP</strong>
 only if 
<strong>HTTPS</strong>
 is not reachable.
</li>
<li>
Burp Suite XML exports can be used as input with 
<code>-l burp-export.xml -im burp</code>
</li>
<li>
The 
<code>-no-fallback</code>
 flag can be used to probe and display both 
<strong>HTTP</strong>
 and 
<strong>HTTPS</strong>
 result.
</li>
<li>
Custom scheme for ports can be defined, for example 
<code>-ports http:443,http:80,https:8443</code>
</li>
<li>
Custom resolver supports multiple protocol (
<strong>doh|tcp|udp</strong>
) in form of 
<code>protocol:resolver:port</code>
 (e.g. 
<code>udp:127.0.0.1:53</code>
)
</li>
<li>
Secret files can be used for domain-based authentication via 
<code>-sf secrets.yaml</code>
. Supported auth types: 
<code>BasicAuth</code>
, 
<code>BearerToken</code>
, 
<code>Header</code>
, 
<code>Cookie</code>
, 
<code>Query</code>
. Example:

<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-ent">id</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">example-auth</span>
<span class="pl-ent">info</span>
:
  
<span class="pl-ent">name</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">Example Auth Config</span>
<span class="pl-ent">static</span>
:
  - 
<span class="pl-ent">type</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">Header</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">domains</span>
:
      - 
<span class="pl-s">api.example.com</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">headers</span>
:
      - 
<span class="pl-ent">key</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">X-API-Key</span>
        <span class="pl-ent">value</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">secret-key-here</span>

  - 
<span class="pl-ent">type</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">BasicAuth</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">domains-regex</span>
:
      - 
<span class="pl-s">
<span class="pl-pds">"</span>
.*
<span class="pl-cce">\\</span>
.internal
<span class="pl-cce">\\</span>
.com$
<span class="pl-pds">"</span>
</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">username</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">admin</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">password</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">secret</span>
</pre>

<li>
The following flags should be used for specific use cases instead of running them as default with other probes:

<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<code>-ports</code>
</li>
<li>
<code>-path</code>
</li>
<li>
